summary: Evening 5xx uptick correlated with SSL ticket rotation and runtime throttle
description: Issue summary: Between ~18:03 and 18:22 UTC on 2026-03-13 we observed an abrupt elevation in 5xx responses for a subset of dedicated customers in us-east-1. Errors were concentrated on streaming and short-payload chat routes. Impact: BrightChat Labs reported a 25% failure rate for in-flight requests during the window; customer-facing sessions observed stream resets and 502/503 responses. Initial hypothesis: coincident SSL session ticket rotation on several load-balancers triggered connection churn that amplified hedged retries and runtime preemption leading to upstream throttling and transient 5xxs.
timeline: 2026-03-13 17:58 UTC - Keystore rotation job scheduled for region us-east-1 (automated daily rotation).
2026-03-13 18:02 UTC - First customer reports of streaming resets to #support. BrightChat Labs contact: ops@brightchat.ai
2026-03-13 18:05 UTC - Apigw error rate metric begins to climb; 502/503 spike detected by SRE alert.
2026-03-13 18:10 UTC - Autoscaler notices ephemeral worker churn; several runtime pods restarted.
2026-03-13 18:18 UTC - SRE temporarily increased api-gateway keepalive and reduced hedged-retry multiplier as mitigation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated tenant in us-east-1 with streaming chat configuration and short prompt sizes.
2) Trigger a keystore/SSL ticket rotation across the ingress layer (internal test job available at confluence runbook).
3) Simulate a moderate hedged-retry client pattern (two rapid retries with 50ms jitter) while gradually increasing concurrent streams to ~200/s.
4) Observe apigw error rate and runtime preemption traces; check kernel/fd and keepalive counters on ingress proxies.

keepalive active connections: dropped ~18% during rotation window
investigation_notes: Initial correlation: rotation timeline lines up with first apigw resets and keepalive drops.
Heap/profile checks on runtime pods do not show OOM. Crash loops appear tied to abrupt connection resets and subsequent preemption under our scheduling policy.
Hypothesis A: SSL ticket rotation caused bulk TLS renegotiations that exposed an accept/handshake backlog on the ingress proxies, amplifying hedged retries and quickly saturating proxy threadpools.

Hypothesis B: Tenants with heavy short-lived streaming sessions experienced increased connection churn which triggered runtime prioritizer to preempt in-flight KV-prefetch tasks leading to downstream 503s.
Checked ndt and kernel fd limits: no system-level fd exhaustion observed on ingress nodes (fd usage peaked but within headroom).

Related prior incidents: SUP-963210 and SUP-472901 show similar patterns where keepalive/handshake churn triggered accept-queue collapse. Link: https://confluence.redwood/company/incidents/keepalive-handshake-collapse
Reproducer: running the confluence repro job with hedged-retry stress reproduces elevated 5xx on staging when keystore rotation is forced.
mitigation_actions: Applied temporary mitigation at 18:18 UTC: increased apigw keepalive timeout from 60s -> 120s for us-east-1 ingress cluster.
Reduced hedged-retry multiplier in routing config for streaming routes for dedicated tenants (rollback ready: config id cfg-20260313-1).
Scoped keystore rotation staging job to avoid rolling rotations across all ingress nodes at once; toggled to staggered rotation as immediate fix.
next_steps: SRE to instrument handshake latency and accept-queue depth with 10s granularity and add flag-based telemetry to correlate keystore rotation events with accept-queue behavior.
Infra to roll a safe guard: perform keystore rotation in two phases (staggered by AZ) rather than global at-same-time in us-east-1.
Runtime team to audit preemption thresholds when connection churn above X% to avoid evicting in-flight short tasks that lead to 5xxs.
Post-incident: schedule a small change window to test rotation strategy on staging with hedged-retry pattern. Owner: Marco Liu. Target: 2026-03-17.
resolution: Workaround applied: staggered keystore rotation and temporary keepalive/hedged-retry tuning reduced 5xx back to baseline by 18:30 UTC. Permanent fix: follow-up action items assigned; awaiting runtime preemption tuning patch and improved rotation runbook.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Customer BrightChat reported elevated errors at 18:03 UTC. Provided initial logs and sample request IDs.
Marco Liu (SRE): Observed apigw threadpool saturation and runtime restarts aligned with rotation. Implemented temporary keepalive increase and hedged-retry reduction.
R&D (J. Park): Reproducer validated on staging when forcing TLS ticket rotation while running short-stream hedged-retry load. Filed follow-up RFC for staggered rotation.
BrightChat Ops (customer): Confirmed reduction in errors after mitigation; asked for permanent timeline and root cause writeup.
